A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Eso-LMs research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison across renumbering, relocation and layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original Eso-LMs perplexity evaluations, ablations, generation-quality comparisons and latency experiments in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results, including LM1B/OWT evaluations, zero-shot likelihoods, ablations and long-context generation timings.

M1.justification: The hybrid objective, shuffled causal attention, unified KV caching and diffusion-then-AR sampling remain unchanged. The 'block sampler' described in v3 is the heuristic already documented in v2 Appendix E.6, rather than an additional procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use LM1B and OWT, the same seven zero-shot evaluation corpora in Table 4, and the same unconditional and long-context generation scenarios. v3 explicitly defers downstream tasks to future work without adding evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding likelihood tables and generation experiments. AR variants, MDLM, BD3-LMs and the other diffusion baselines retain their roles; moving baseline citations out of Table 1 does not remove comparisons.

E3.justification: Splits, preprocessing, model configurations, training budgets, metrics and sampling protocols are retained. v3's added mention of finer T values at alpha_eval=1 describes settings already reported in v2 Table 11, including T=32, 64, 256 and 4096.

E4.justification: Both retain the batch-split ablation, Eso-LMs (A) attention ablation, importance-weighting sweeps, BD3-LM sampling-control analysis, improved-sampler comparison and generated examples. The new Appendix E subsection headings largely organize existing analyses and relocated plots.

E5.justification: Both report ten timing trials in Section 5.2 and means with standard deviations over five runs in Tables 9–10. Monte Carlo sampling, low-discrepancy estimation and importance-weighting sample counts are unchanged; no new uncertainty-reporting procedure appears.

E6.justification: Tables 1–13 retain their result entries and numerical values, and matched plots and generated sample texts are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains alpha_0=1 perplexities of 31.65 on LM1B and 29.31 on OWT, while Table 9 retains 82.1-second Eso-LMs latency at length 8192.

T1.justification: Appendix B.3 substantially expands the mathematical support for hybrid likelihood estimation. v2 states the hybrid importance-weighted theorem with a one-sentence proof; v3 adds an alternative NELBO, a Bernoulli clean-token subset construction, an explicit permutation distribution, and Lemmas B.2–B.3 with derivations supporting the retained theorem, now B.4.

C1.justification: v3 qualifies the highlighted likelihood contribution as '(asymptotically) exact,' whereas v2's contribution list omitted that qualification. The principal interpolation, speed-quality frontier and 14–65×/3–4× speedup claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly identifies downstream tasks as future work and conditions its recommendation to train with alpha_train=1 on a compute budget. Existing interpretations and limitations concerning causal attention, perplexity, training overhead and delayed KV reuse remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3 newly specifies training on nodes of eight H200 GPUs and single-GPU throughput and latency benchmarking. Section 5 adds approximately 9K H200 GPU hours for pretraining and ablations. Previously reported runtimes, implementation code and resource-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Dong et al. (2024) for FlexAttention and removes the d2 and d1 citations and discussion of subsequent RL work building on Eso-LMs. It also revises concurrent caching work's description from reuse within blocks to reuse from previous blocks. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The six-section main narrative is retained, with an expanded title, prose refinements and clearer likelihood exposition. Scheduler pseudocode and attention definitions move to Appendix B. v3 adds an Impact Statement and removes the populated contents listing and Appendix F's LLM-writing disclosure.

P2.justification: v3 substantially redesigns presentation: the main text and references become two-column, Figure 1 is transposed and loses its schematic Pareto panel, and retained training-speed and generative-perplexity plots move into Appendix E. Figures and tables are extensively resized and redistributed.

improvement.justification: The expanded Appendix B.3 derivation makes the hybrid likelihood argument easier to assess, while explicit GPU counts improve reproducibility and the asymptotic qualification improves claim precision. These provide a limited net gain. Finite-K results still carry 'exact' labels, and removal of the populated contents listing and RL-related context modestly reduces navigation and contextual completeness.
